lead: Based on what you told me, your number one constraint is:
h1: You’re [[educating buyers on your sales page]], instead of selling to them.
fix_h: Save your sales page for buyers to **confirm their decision**, not to make it from scratch.
arr_k: What they’re thinking as they land on your sales page
now_say: “Let me see what this actually is.”
now_note: They read, compare tabs, and leave to think about it.
fix_say: “I already know this is for me. Where do I buy?”
fix_note: The page is for the last few questions.
how_h: To turn more of your visitors into buyers:
fan_tap: Tap the card for the next one
how1: **Pre-educate before the sales page.** Show your process, your difference and your price range in your emails and content, so the page only has to answer the last few questions.
how2: **Personalize the pre-sales experience.** You attract two different personas, each with different use cases, objections and reasons to buy, so show each one the right features, testimonials and answers before they ever reach your sales page.
how3: **Filter misfits early, without lowering your price.** Stop hoping a sales page will convert someone who was never the right fit, and point the right buyers to the offer built for them.
lens: Through the **Revenue Per Visitor™** lens, this raises buyers in the first 14 days. It sits in Speed to Decision™, quadrant 3 of the Compounding Revenue Per Visitor™ OS.
cta: Show me how to turn more of my visitors into buyers
up_next: Next question: What have you already tried to improve your revenue?
